ig_carousel_topic.topic: Reading line movement, what it tells you the public can't see
ig_carousel_topic.slide1_text:
The line moved. Now what?
Line movement is data.
Most bettors ignore it.
ig_carousel_topic.slide2_text:
Common assumption: if a line moves against a team, the public is betting the other side.
Sometimes true. Usually incomplete.
The public moves lines. Sharp money moves them differently.
ig_carousel_topic.slide3_text:
Sportsbooks shade lines toward the public. Sharp action forces corrections.
If a team opens -3 and climbs to -4.5 while most tickets are on the other side, that's a signal.
The books are reacting to money, not ticket count.
ig_carousel_topic.slide4_text:
Real example structure:
Team A opens -3. 65% of tickets on Team B.
Line moves to -3.5 anyway.
That means large-dollar action came in on Team A. The books adjusted. Ticket count didn't drive it.
ig_carousel_topic.slide5_text:
You can't see every bet placed. But you can read what the books are telling you.
Reverse line movement is one of the cleaner signals available to retail bettors.
Pair it with closing line value and you have a real framework.
